threads.body:
Dropping the whole `mcp.network.protocol.attributes` group removes more than what actually varies within a session.

`jsonrpc.protocol.version` and `network.protocol.name` are fixed for the lifetime of a session, and the transport *family* (stdio vs HTTP) is too - only `tcp` vs `quic` and the HTTP version can change between operations. Losing the stdio-vs-HTTP split takes away what is probably the most useful dimension on session duration, since the two have completely different lifetime distributions.

Suggest keeping the session-stable attributes and narrowing the removal to `network.transport` + `network.protocol.version`

threads.body:
Removing `server.address`/`server.port` is not supported by the motivation - the MCP endpoint is fixed for a session; a client cannot move a session to another server.

Without them the session-duration metric cannot be broken down per server, and cannot be joined with the client operation metrics and spans that keep these attributes.

This is standard OTel histogram behavior - measurements above the last boundary always fall into the last (`+Inf`) bucket - so it does not need to be restated on individual metrics. Please drop the sentence here and at line 997.

Also, "overflow bucket" is not the right term: in OTel, overflow refers to the attribute set produced when a cardinality limit is hit.
